name: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
positioning: Lagoon resort of overwater bungalows and beach villas with Mount Otemanu as its backdrop, formerly Le Meridien Bora Bora
best_for: Honeymooners wanting an overwater bungalow with a plunge pool
Travelers interested in Polynesian culture and sea turtle conservation
Families or groups wanting villas with lagoon access

facts.text: Mount Otemanu serves as the backdrop to the resort.
The resort offers the most overwater bungalows on the island.
Overwater bungalows have a modern design with Polynesian accents.
Villas have a freestanding bathtub with lagoon views.
Every visit to the Heavenly Spa includes the Three Stones Ritual.
Sunrise yoga is held once a week on the main beach facing Mount Otemanu.
A weekly Polynesian show celebrates traditional dress, dance, music and food.
Maere's head chef creates a new themed menu every evening.
Guests can snorkel in the lagoon, paddleboard and kayak, and play beach volleyball, badminton and beach tennis.
The resort was previously known as Le Meridien Bora Bora.

highlights.text: Overwater bungalows have the largest glass-paneled floors in Bora Bora for viewing marine life.
Sixty-two overwater bungalows and villas have their own saltwater plunge pool.
Guests can encounter rescued and rehabbing turtles at the Eco Centre.
The resort has an infinity pool with Otemanu views and the Te Ava swim-up bar.
Cultural classes include coconut palm weaving, shell craft, flower crown weaving and Tahitian dance.

considerations.text: WhataHotel notes the remote island location requires flight connections.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing that reflects the Bora Bora destination.
